title: ci: add artifact signing, SBOM generation, and provenance release manifests for private-installer
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments require auditable, signed release artifacts and machine-readable provenance to satisfy compliance and to enable secure offline installs. This PR wires artifact signing and provenance generation into the private-installer release flow, produces SBOMs, and emits a set of release manifests used by the installer/upgrade tooling.

What this PR does: 1) Adds CI steps to build installer artifacts (helm chart tgz, installer binaries, terraform modules), generate SBOMs (Syft), and create in-toto provenance statements and cosign signatures. 2) Produces a release-manifests/ directory with per-release YAML that includes artifact URLs, SBOM references, signatures, and build metadata. 3) Updates the release upload step to store artifacts and signatures in our release S3 bucket using kms-encrypted uploads and to publish a signed top-level manifest. 4) Adds verification helper scripts used by private install automation to fetch and verify signatures and provenance prior to deploy. 5) Minor Helm values cleanup to ensure chart artifact reproducibility.

Checklist: - [x] Build artifacts in CI and attach to release - [x] Generate SBOMs using syft - [x] Produce signed provenance (in-toto) and cosign signatures - [x] Upload artifacts + signatures to release bucket with KMS - [x] Emit release-manifests/*.yml consumable by private-installer/upgrade tooling - [x] Add docs section describing verification flow

Rollout: This PR is backwards compatible: older installer releases are unchanged. The release pipeline emits the same artifacts plus the extra signature/provenance files. Private deployment automation will be upgraded to verify signatures in a follow-up PR (ENG-1620).

review_comments: Miguel Torres (reviewer): Can we ensure the cosign keys are only available to the release runner and that we use a KMS-backed key? Also request to add TTL for artifacts in the bucket.
Author (Asha Patel): Key access is limited to the release role; we switched to KMS-wrapped keys and added an S3 lifecycle rule for signed artifacts. Added notes in docs/release.md.

Lina Chen (reviewer): E2E failed on the first run due to a timeout in the integration suite. Please make the SBOM step timeout friendly or run it after deploy stage. Also request reproducible builds note.
Author (Asha Patel): Moved SBOM generation to post-build step and added deterministic flag to Helm pack command; added CI retry for flaky network steps. Re-ran CI and fixed timeouts.
Samir Kulkarni (approver): Verified signatures locally using the verify script; looks good. Approving for merge with squash.
ci_checks: github-actions/release.yml: sbom-generation -> pass (rerun after timeout fix)
release_notes: CI: release pipeline now produces SBOMs, in-toto provenance statements, and cosign signatures for private-installer artifacts.
Release manifests: added release-manifests/{version}.yml that lists artifact URLs, SBOM locations, and signature files for offline installers and upgrade tooling.
Security: signing keys are KMS-backed and upload uses kms-encrypted S3 put-object calls.
notes_for_ops: The release pipeline writes artifacts to s3://redwood-private-installer-releases/{version}/ with a top-level manifest.yml and a signed manifest.yml.sig. The verification helper script scripts/verify-release.sh assumes AWS role 'release-uploader' or local cosign public key set via COSIGN_PUB. See docs/release.md for verification steps.
